config.title: Write controlled input and live preview

intro.title: Write controlled input and live preview
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web application that displays a live preview of text as you type it into an input field. You will learn how to create a controlled input component, where the input's value is managed by React state, ensuring the UI always reflects the current data. The core concept involves using React's useState hook to store the input value and updating it with an onChange event handler. This exercise will help you understand the connection between state, user input, and real-time UI updates in a React application.
intro.usecase: Controlled inputs with live preview are essential for creating responsive, user-friendly interfaces in modern web applications. This pattern appears in real-time form validation where users see immediate feedback as they type, such as password strength indicators or email format checkers. It's also crucial in dashboard filters where changing a dropdown instantly updates charts and data visualizations, and in content editors where text formatting or image adjustments show live previews. Developers implement this daily in search interfaces with autocomplete suggestions, configuration panels with instant previews, and any interactive UI where user input should trigger immediate visual feedback.

objectives: Implement a controlled input component that synchronizes user input with component state
Initialize state variables to store input values and preview content
Bind input event handlers to update state when users type in form fields
Construct a live preview display that renders state changes in real-time
Configure bidirectional data flow between input elements and state management
Manipulate DOM elements to reflect controlled input values dynamically
Integrate state updates with rendering logic to maintain consistent UI state

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary React APIs imported to create a component and manage state.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and the useState hook from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns null. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an App component defined that returns null.
successCriteria: The App component is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your App component returns null explicitly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named App that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize state for the input value
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, call useState to create a state variable named 'inputValue' and its setter function. Initialize it with an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [inputValue, setInputValue] = useState('');
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your App component will have a state variable 'inputValue' initialized to an empty string, ready to store text from an input field.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called inside the App component, creating a state variable named 'inputValue' and its setter function, initialized with an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've called useState with an empty string as the initial value and named the variable 'inputValue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the App component, use useState to create a state variable called 'inputValue' initialized to an empty string.

steps.title: Define the input change handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named handleInputChange that takes an event parameter and calls setInputValue with event.target.value.
steps.hint: Define the function before the return statement. Use event.target.value to get the current input value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleInputChange function is defined inside the App component, ready to update the state when the input changes.
successCriteria: The handleInputChange function is defined, takes an event parameter, and calls setInputValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes an event parameter and calls setInputValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to define a function named handleInputChange that updates the state with the input's current value.

steps.title: Return the component's JSX structure
steps.instruction: Change the App component's return statement to return a JSX fragment (<>...</>) containing a single div element.
steps.hint: Replace the current 'return null;' with a JSX fragment that wraps a div element. The fragment syntax uses empty angle brackets.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns a JSX fragment containing a div element, providing the basic structure for the UI.
successCriteria: The App component returns a JSX fragment (<>...</>) with a div element inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a JSX fragment (<>...</>) with a div element inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a JSX fragment containing a div element. Check that you're using the correct syntax for JSX fragments.

steps.title: Add a heading to the structure
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add an h1 element with the text 'Live Preview App'.
steps.hint:
Add

Live Preview App

inside the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div containing an h1 heading with the text 'Live Preview App'.
successCriteria: An h1 element with the text 'Live Preview App' is present inside the div in the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the heading to your app interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an h1 element with the exact text 'Live Preview App' inside the div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading wasn't added correctly. Check that you have an h1 element with 'Live Preview App' inside the div in your return statement.

steps.title: Add the text input element
steps.instruction: Below the heading, add an input element of type 'text'. Set its value attribute to the state variable (inputValue).
steps.hint: Add an <input> tag inside the <div> after the <h1>. Use the value prop to bind it to inputValue.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: a controlled text input
<input type="text" value={someState} />
steps.expectedOutcome: A text input field appears in the UI, with its value controlled by the inputValue state.
successCriteria: An <input type="text"> element is added below the heading, with its value attribute set to {inputValue}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input, but make sure its value attribute is set to {inputValue} to create a controlled input.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or not correctly set up. Add an <input type="text"> with value={inputValue}.

steps.title: Wire the input's onChange event
steps.instruction: Add an onChange attribute to the input element and set it to the handleInputChange function.
steps.hint: In JSX, add onChange={handleInputChange} to the input element to connect the event to your handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring an input event
<input type="text" onChange={handleChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will have an onChange attribute that calls the handleInputChange function when the input value changes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the onChange attribute is set to handleInputChange without parentheses (e.g., onChange={handleInputChange}).
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element should have an onChange attribute that calls the handleInputChange function. Check your syntax and try again.

steps.title: Add a paragraph for the live preview
steps.instruction: Below the input element, add a paragraph element that displays the current input value for live preview.
steps.hint:
Add a

tag after the input. Inside the paragraph, you can display the inputValue state variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a paragraph to display text

Current text: {textValue}
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph element should appear below the input and display the current value of inputValue.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added after the input element and displays the inputValue state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the current inputValue state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element is missing or doesn't display the input value. Try adding a

tag with {inputValue} inside.

steps.title: Display the state value in the preview
steps.instruction: Inside the paragraph element, after the 'Preview: ' text, insert the inputValue state variable to display the live text.
steps.hint: Use curly braces {} to embed the JavaScript expression containing inputValue within the paragraph.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a variable in JSX

Current value: {someVariable}
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph will display the current input value as you type, creating a live preview effect.
successCriteria: The paragraph element contains the inputValue variable after the 'Preview: ' text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the inputValue variable inside the paragraph after 'Preview: '.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph should display the current input value. Check that you've inserted inputValue after 'Preview: ' using curly braces.
